## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Saṅgahavāra* ("The classes of offenses to which each rule belongs") is an analytical section of the *Parivāra*, the final treatise of the Theravāda *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The chapter systematically examines monastic infractions, defining which rules may fall under the heading or classification of other rules [SuttaCentral]. A complete English translation of the section has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus identifies extensive internal reuse within the Pāli canon, recording 123 matching passages shared across 17 other texts, predominantly situated within the *Parivāra* itself [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4; 30 matches), followed by the *Saṅgahitavāra* (Pvr 1.12), the *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), the *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 2.8), and another homonymous chapter titled *Saṅgahavāra* (Pvr 2.12) [DharmaNexus]. Further formulaic parallels connect it to adjacent sections such as the *Vipattivāra* (Pvr 2.3), *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 2.2), and the commentary *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus detects no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
None of the passages located in the reference search discuss this Vinaya text; occurrences of the title *saṅgahavāra* in the searched corpus pertain instead to the summary section of the Abhidhamma *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, while other matching references pertain to unrelated compendia containing the word *saṅgaha*, primarily the *Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha*.
